artifacts.summary: 7-phase, 7-hour comment-and-docstring-only sweep replacing the historical TM/BX f/c/dc subscripts with the paper's z/d/r vocabulary, partitioned into mechanical rename, editorial rewrites of 12 retracted-claim passages, and a canonical two-base-systems mapping paragraph.

user_decision.question: The task description says the mapping paragraph should describe this repository's TM (BaseLanguage, H/G primitive) as the paper's Past/Future footnote system, but research verified that footnote is entirely commented out in the live possible_worlds.tex (lines 1331-1341), pending the non-axiomatizability result. How should the mapping paragraph describe the BaseLanguage systems?
options: Say they have no paper name today, plus one sentence noting the paper carries a commented-out Past/Future footnote pending the non-axiomatizability result
Say flatly that TM, TM_z, TM_d and TM_r on the BaseLanguage side have no paper name, with no mention of the commented-out footnote
Follow the task description literally and describe them as the footnote's Past/Future system, treating the footnote as forthcoming
user_decision.recommended: Say they have no paper name today, plus one sentence noting the paper carries a commented-out Past/Future footnote pending the non-axiomatizability result

memory_candidates.content: Planning a rename sweep of prose that characterizes an external paper: partition by claim class, not by token count. Class A (mechanical) is files whose occurrences are pure labels — safe for scripted literal replacement. Class B (editorial) is passages that assert something about the source which the source's revision retracted: verbatim quotations of deleted text, 'gap'/'open question' paragraphs the revision closed, and two-name contrasts whose names collapse to one (a naive sed there yields the nonsense 'this is X, not X'). Class C is additive (a canonical mapping passage placed first, so every later phase references rather than reinvents wording). Two structural rules make the phases parallelizable and safe: give each phase a disjoint file territory even when a single file carries both mechanical and editorial work, and write the completeness grep scoped to live source directories — a repo-wide grep can never pass because the task's own specs/ artifacts quote every retired name by construction. Cite source anchors, never source line numbers, in the rewritten prose.
